job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

response.passage: In our science lab, we set up a model to study atmospheric conditions. We placed a thermometer in a shaded area to record the daily maximum temperature, which we observed consistently peaks in the mid-afternoon rather than at noon. Next, we used a wet-bulb thermometer to measure moisture in the air, confirming that humidity is present even on dry, sunny days when no rain is falling. We then discussed how animals survive in extreme environments. We learned that polar bears, which inhabit the Arctic, have thick white fur that provides camouflage against the snow, helping them hunt prey effectively. In contrast, penguins are found exclusively in the Antarctic. Finally, we explored air movement by observing smoke moving toward a low-pressure zone. We discovered that air always flows from high-pressure areas to low-pressure areas, which explains why wind speeds increase as the pressure difference between two regions grows. This experiment helped us distinguish between daily weather changes and the long-term climate patterns of a region, showing that a single cold day does not disprove the reality of global warming.
response.summary: This classroom experiment demonstrates how daily temperature and humidity are measured while clarifying animal adaptations and the physics of wind. It also distinguishes between short-term weather events and long-term climate trends.
